title: Musical family in New Orleans and early arranging with Clyde Kerr
summary: Born 1930 in New Orleans into a musical family; plays trumpet professionally from 12-13; learns arranging from Clyde Kerr Sr. at Xavier Prep and from stock arrangements, and forms a trio with the Johnson brothers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was born in 1930 in New Orleans, Louisiana. My family is a musical, have a musical background. My father played banjo and guitar. He did a couple of, before I was born, he did a couple of things with Louis Armstrong, so he claims. I have a brother that plays drum. He plays with the Dixieland groups in town. His name is Leo. I have an older brother named Sid. He plays trumpet. He does a lot of little jobs in ballrooms and MCs and all that kind of stuff. And I had uncles that played, one played piano, had some that played saxophone. My brother played trumpet. My father played D-banjo. The one brother played drums and had a lot of friends. My mother sang. I had an uncle that sang. We used to get together every Sunday. We used to have a really good time musically and playing in all that kind of jazz. So I came up with that atmosphere. And I played trumpet at the time. I was fairly good, but I had experiences from 12 to 13 playing professional, going out with my brothers, different locations, out of town for picnics, family affairs and all of that. So I really had a good time during those days. And like I said, a lot of musical training that way, you know, experience wise. I went to Xavier Prep and I met one of my oldest friends, Mr. Clyde Cuss, Sr. He was teaching at Xavier Prep at the time. I was in a band. And he used to come in the classroom and do a lot of writing, writing for bands. He had a band and a group. And he was writing. And this was my first experience as far as arranging is concerned. Because I would imagine that I was like anyone else and never had the opportunity to study arranging. I never knew what it was to be truthful. Whether it is an arrangement. I know I used to read notes, but who put those notes and all that together, I never knew. So he used to come to the classroom and he used to give us some studies and he would sit behind his desk and he would write. I used to sneak up behind him and find out what he was doing. So, you know, he was very, a very nice person. He explained to me what he was doing and what this is called arranging and all this kind of thing. So I took an interest in it and I started getting books. I used to buy stock arrangements. A stock arrangement is an arrangement that they sell in the music stores. And they had the arrangement, dance music for different dance, you know, for dance bands and things like that. So I used to buy that, buy the arrangement and I used to analyze the arrangements and say, and I got my, my arranging from that sauce plus, of course, Mr. Curl. You know, if I never understood, some things I never understood, I would ask him and he would be very kind to take the time to explain what it was. From that period, I got into playing with different people in the school. I used to have a guy named Placid, not Placid Adam, Placid Johnson, I believe. Right now, him and his brother. Placid, yeah. Placid Johnson, right. Well, he used to have a band, he and, he had a brother that played piano. Raymond played piano. Raymond, okay. Good, I'm glad you're here because I forget those kind of things. I can't remember names from yesterday, less known in the 30s, the 40s. And we had a group and it was something like, it was a trio, something along the lines of Nat King Cole Trio and things like that. But it was just us three.
